stories.title: Implement typed Skyscanner API client
stories.description: Create src/skyscanner/client.ts that wraps the Skyscanner RapidAPI. The client must: (1) export a SkyscannerClient class whose constructor accepts { apiKey: string }; if apiKey is omitted, fall back to the RAPIDAPI_KEY environment variable — throw a descriptive Error if neither is present; (2) implement searchFlights(params: SearchParams): Promise<FlightResult[]> using the Node.js 18+ global fetch (no third-party HTTP library); (3) export TypeScript interfaces SearchParams { origin: string; destination: string; date: string; adults?: number } and FlightResult { price: number; currency: string; airline: string; departure: string; arrival: string; duration: number; stops: number }; (4) throw on HTTP 4xx/5xx responses, including the status code in the message; (5) throw a descriptive parse error when the response body does not match the expected shape. Also create src/skyscanner/client.test.ts with vitest tests that mock the global fetch — no real network calls. (6) Support an explicit mock mode: when the environment variable MOCK_SKYSCANNER_API is set to the exact string 'true', searchFlights must return deterministic fixture FlightResult[] data WITHOUT making any network call (no fetch invocation at all) — this is an opt-in-only behavior; when MOCK_SKYSCANNER_API is unset, empty, or any value other than 'true', searchFlights must behave exactly as it does today (real fetch call, real failures surfaced, no silent fallback to mock data on real-call failure).

When apiKey is passed as an empty string ('') to the constructor, SkyscannerClient throws the same missing-key Error as when apiKey is omitted entirely
When RAPIDAPI_KEY is set to an empty string in the environment and no apiKey is provided to the constructor, SkyscannerClient throws the missing-key Error
When an apiKey is provided to the constructor and RAPIDAPI_KEY is also set in the environment, the constructor-provided apiKey takes precedence

When the API response body is malformed or missing expected fields, searchFlights rejects with a descriptive parse/validation Error

When fetch throws a network-level error (e.g., DNS resolution failure, connection refused), searchFlights rejects with an Error — this is distinct from HTTP status-code error handling and does not produce a FlightResult[]

When MOCK_SKYSCANNER_API env var equals exactly 'true', searchFlights resolves with a deterministic, non-empty FlightResult[] fixture (at least 2 results, valid shape matching the FlightResult interface, varying price so cheapest-selection logic in SKY-004 is exercisable) and does not invoke fetch

stories.title: Implement flight search CLI entry point with formatted table output
stories.description: Create `src/cli.ts` — a standalone Node entry point that accepts flight search arguments via `process.argv` and prints results as an aligned table. Parse flags manually (no commander, no yargs, zero new runtime deps). Require `RAPIDAPI_KEY` env var; exit 1 with a human-readable message if absent. Instantiate `SkyscannerClient` from `src/skyscanner/client.ts` (SKY-002), call `searchFlights` forwarding all parsed arguments including adults count, and render results in a dynamically-padded table with columns: Airline | Price | Departure | Arrival | Duration | Stops. Column widths are determined by the widest value in each column (including the header). A separator row of hyphen characters must appear between the header and data rows. Price is right-aligned and prefixed with the currency symbol returned by the API (default £ if absent); all other columns are left-aligned. If no flights are returned print `No flights found.` and exit 0. On any thrown error print the message to stderr and exit 1. Create `src/cli.test.ts` covering argument validation, successful render, empty-result render, missing env var, and error handling using vitest with `SkyscannerClient` mocked at the module boundary. The compiled output must be invokable as `node dist/cli.js ...` after `tsc`; `tsconfig.json` must have `outDir` set to `dist` and emit CommonJS-compatible output.
acceptanceCriteria: Delegated to split children: SKY-003-A, SKY-003-B

specification.coordinatorNotes: Requirements are already well-elaborated with 14 clear ACs. Primary risks are testability (table alignment verification strategy, process.exit mocking in vitest) and edge-case hardening (currency symbol fallback, separator-row width exactness, stderr/stdout isolation in error paths). speckit reviews for security (env var not leaked in output) and test coverage gaps; openspec not needed — no ambiguity in requirements.

stories.title: Build Express REST API with /health, /search, /cheapest, and static dashboard endpoints
stories.description: Create src/server.ts — an Express HTTP server that exposes: (1) GET /health → { status: 'ok', uptime: number }, (2) GET /search?from=LHR&to=JFK&date=2026-08-01&adults=1 → { flights: FlightResult[], count: number, searchedAt: string }, (3) GET /cheapest?from=LHR&to=JFK&date=2026-08-01 → the single cheapest FlightResult or 404 JSON { error: string } if none found, (4) GET / → serves src/public/index.html by reading the file at runtime (e.g. fs.readFileSync) — the handler must NOT hardcode a separate inline HTML string that merely happens to match; content and implementation must not be able to diverge. Server reads PORT from env (default 3000); reads RAPIDAPI_KEY from env and passes to SkyscannerClient. If RAPIDAPI_KEY is absent at startup all API routes (/search, /cheapest) return 503 { error: 'RAPIDAPI_KEY not configured' }; /health and / are never gated. The listen() call must be guarded so importing `app` in tests does not bind a port. Add 'start' script in package.json pointing to 'node dist/server.js'. Install supertest and @types/supertest. Create src/server.test.ts using vitest + supertest with at least 8 tests covering the scenarios in acceptance criteria. Depends on SKY-002 (SkyscannerClient and FlightResult type must exist before this story is started). The build script must copy src/public/ (or equivalent static assets) into dist/public/ as part of `npm run build`, since tsc alone does not copy non-.ts files — the file path used by the /  route handler must resolve correctly both under `tsx src/server.ts` (dev) and `node dist/server.js` (built).
acceptanceCriteria: Given the server module is imported in a test file, When no HTTP request is made, Then no port is bound and no EADDRINUSE error occurs; the named `app` export is an Express instance usable with supertest
Given any RAPIDAPI_KEY state, When GET /health is requested, Then the response is HTTP 200 with JSON body containing `status: 'ok'` and `uptime` as a positive number
Given any RAPIDAPI_KEY state, When GET / is requested, Then the response is HTTP 200 with Content-Type text/html and the body contains the contents of src/public/index.html served at runtime

Given RAPIDAPI_KEY is configured and valid params (from, to, date), When GET /search?from=LHR&to=JFK&date=2026-08-01&adults=1 is requested, Then the response is HTTP 200 with JSON body containing `flights` (array), `count` (number), and `searchedAt` (ISO 8601 string)

Given RAPIDAPI_KEY is configured, When GET /search is requested without `from`, `to`, or `date` query params, Then the response is HTTP 400 with JSON body containing an `error` field describing the missing required parameters
Given RAPIDAPI_KEY is configured, When GET /search is requested with a non-numeric `adults` param (e.g. adults=abc), Then the response is HTTP 400 with JSON body containing an `error` field
Given RAPIDAPI_KEY is configured, When GET /search is requested without an `adults` param, Then `adults` defaults to 1 in the search request and the response is HTTP 200

Given RAPIDAPI_KEY is configured and valid params, When GET /cheapest?from=LHR&to=JFK&date=2026-08-01 is requested, Then the response is HTTP 200 with a single FlightResult object that has the lowest price among all results
Given RAPIDAPI_KEY is configured and valid params but SkyscannerClient returns zero results, When GET /cheapest is requested, Then the response is HTTP 404 with JSON body `{ error: string }`
Given RAPIDAPI_KEY is configured, When GET /cheapest is requested without `from`, `to`, or `date` query params, Then the response is HTTP 400 with JSON body containing an `error` field
Given RAPIDAPI_KEY is configured, When GET /cheapest is requested without an `adults` param, Then `adults` defaults to 1 and the response is HTTP 200 (if results exist)
Given RAPIDAPI_KEY is absent at server startup, When GET /search or GET /cheapest is requested, Then the response is HTTP 503 with JSON body `{ error: 'RAPIDAPI_KEY not configured' }`
Given RAPIDAPI_KEY is absent at server startup, When GET /health or GET / is requested, Then the response is unaffected (200 as normal)

Given RAPIDAPI_KEY is configured, When SkyscannerClient throws an error during /search or /cheapest, Then the response is HTTP 500 with JSON body `{ error: string }` and the server remains running and responsive to subsequent requests

Given the FlightResult type from SKY-002, When the server returns flight data on /search or /cheapest, Then each flight object conforms to the FlightResult type structure defined in SKY-002 (not a locally redeclared type)

Given GET /search or GET /cheapest is requested with query params containing HTML or script tags (e.g. from=<script>alert(1)</script>), Then the response does not reflect unsanitized input and no unescaped script content appears in the JSON response body
Given GET /search or GET /cheapest is requested with `adults` set to 0 or a negative number, Then the response is HTTP 400 with an `error` field
Given GET /search or GET /cheapest is requested with a `date` in an invalid format (e.g. date=not-a-date), Then the response is HTTP 400 with an `error` field

Given src/public/index.html, When rendered in a browser, Then it contains a header, a search form with from/to/date/adults inputs, a results area, and client-side JavaScript that calls GET /search without page reload

Given src/public/index.html, When rendered in a browser, Then the page includes a lang attribute on the html element, labels associated with form inputs, and meaningful heading hierarchy for accessibility
Given `npm run build` is executed, Then dist/server.js is produced and src/public/ is copied into dist/public/; `npm run build && npm run start` starts a working server on the configured port
Given the package.json start script, When `npm run start` is executed, Then it runs `node dist/server.js`

Given the test suite, When `vitest run` is executed, Then at least 8 tests pass covering: /health 200, / 200 with HTML, /search 200 with valid params, /search 400 with missing params, /cheapest 200, /cheapest 404 with no results, /search 503 without RAPIDAPI_KEY, /cheapest 500 on SkyscannerClient error
Given the project, When `npx tsc --noEmit` is executed, Then it exits 0 with no type errors

specification.coordinatorNotes: Most complex story with 23 ACs spanning Express routing, static file serving with runtime file read (no hardcoded HTML), build pipeline (public/ copy to dist/), listen() guard patterns (ESM vs CJS), dashboard SPA with client-side fetch, and 503 key-gating middleware. openspec elaborates build pipeline contract, listen guard implementation, and dashboard JS behavior; speckit hardens security (503 gating bypass, error message leakage, unhandled rejection paths), testability (supertest + vi.mock patterns), and flags gaps in static-file error handling (missing index.html at runtime).

stories.title: Implement SkyscannerClient class and TypeScript interfaces
stories.description: Create src/skyscanner/client.ts with the SkyscannerClient class, SearchParams/FlightResult interfaces, global-fetch-based searchFlights method, constructor key resolution with env-var fallback, error handling for HTTP errors and malformed responses, private apiKey field, and explicit MOCK_SKYSCANNER_API='true' mock mode that returns deterministic fixture data without calling fetch.
acceptanceCriteria: SkyscannerClient class is exported with constructor signature constructor({ apiKey }: { apiKey?: string })
SearchParams interface is exported with exactly: origin: string, destination: string, date: string, adults?: number
FlightResult interface is exported with exactly: price: number, currency: string, airline: string, departure: string, arrival: string, duration: number, stops: number
searchFlights uses the Node.js 18+ global fetch exclusively — no axios, node-fetch, or other HTTP dependency imported
apiKey is stored as a private field (private or # prefix) on the SkyscannerClient instance and is not publicly readable; constructor-provided apiKey takes precedence over RAPIDAPI_KEY env var
When apiKey is omitted or empty string and RAPIDAPI_KEY is unset or empty string, constructor throws an Error whose message references the missing key
HTTP 4xx/5xx → searchFlights rejects with an Error that includes the status code in its message; the error message does not contain the apiKey value anywhere

Malformed/missing-fields response → searchFlights rejects with a descriptive parse/validation Error; MOCK_SKYSCANNER_API='true' → returns deterministic FlightResult[] fixture (≥2 results, valid shape, varying prices) without calling fetch; any other value → real fetch; real failures are never silently replaced with mock data

stories.title: Implement flight search CLI entry point (src/cli.ts)
stories.description: Create `src/cli.ts` — a standalone Node entry point that accepts flight search arguments via `process.argv` and prints results as an aligned table. Parse flags manually (no commander, no yargs, zero new runtime deps). Require `RAPIDAPI_KEY` env var; exit 1 with a human-readable message if absent. Instantiate `SkyscannerClient` from `src/skyscanner/client.ts` (SKY-002), call `searchFlights` forwarding all parsed arguments including adults count, and render results in a dynamically-padded table. The compiled output must be invokable as `node dist/cli.js ...` after `tsc`.
acceptanceCriteria: `src/cli.ts` exists and `tsc --noEmit` reports zero errors; `tsconfig.json` sets `outDir` to `dist` and emits CommonJS-compatible output invocable as `node dist/cli.js`

Flags `--from`, `--to`, `--date` are required; if any is absent the CLI prints a usage hint to stderr (showing correct flag names) and exits code 2; `--date` must match `YYYY-MM-DD` or exits 2 with a human-readable message to stderr before any network call
Optional `--adults` flag defaults to 1 when omitted; a non-integer, ≤0, or non-numeric value causes exit code 2 with a human-readable message to stderr
The parsed `adults` value is forwarded as an argument to `SkyscannerClient.searchFlights` — the flag is not silently dropped
If `RAPIDAPI_KEY` env var is unset or empty, CLI prints 'Error: RAPIDAPI_KEY environment variable is required' to stderr and exits 1 before making any network call

When `searchFlights` resolves with one or more results, stdout contains: a header row (Airline, Price, Departure, Arrival, Duration, Stops), a separator row of hyphens matching each column width, and one data row per result; all columns padded to the widest value in that column (including header); all columns left-aligned except Price which is right-aligned
Price column values are prefixed with the currency symbol from the API response; if the API response omits a currency symbol, £ is used as the fallback

When `searchFlights` resolves with an empty array, stdout contains exactly the line `No flights found.` and process exits 0; when `searchFlights` rejects, the error message is written to stderr, stdout is empty, and process exits 1
